newsitem.title: GUATEMALA: Guatemala rebels halt propaganda to boost peace.
newsitem.headline: Guatemala rebels halt propaganda to boost peace.

text.p: Guatemala's leftist rebels, in a gesture aimed at boosting the country's troubled peace process, said on Monday they would suspend armed propaganda campaigns and called for stalled talks with the government to resume as soon as possible.

Peace negotiations between the government and the Guatemalan National Revolutionary Unit (URNG) were suspended by the government last week after a guerrilla commander was arrested as a suspect in a kidnapping.

"The URNG General Command declares that it has decided unilaterally to suspend armed propaganda activities," URNG leaders exiled in Mexico City, who form the team that negotiates with the Guatemalan government, said in a statement.

Even as peace talks to end Guatemala's 36-year civil war have accelerated recently, the URNG has continued to propagandize. Small groups of armed guerrillas frequently enter villages or markets to give speeches and distribute pamphlets.

Peace talks, which have been going on since 1991, were supposed to culminate in December with the signing of a definitive peace treaty to end a war that has left 100,000 dead and more than 40,000 disappeared.
The government and URNG leaders were scheduled to meet in Mexico City last Tuesday for the third session in a round of talks regarding the future of guerrilla fighters.

But the session was called off on Monday when the government announced the Oct. 19 arrest of Rafael Valdizon, accused of kidnapping wealthy, 86-year-old Olga Alvarado de Novella Aug. 25 and asking for millions of dollars in ransom.
Valdizon negotiated his freedom in exchange for the freedom of Alvarado, who is confined to a wheelchair.
Valdizon was the second in command of one of the four rebel factions that make up the URNG, but the guerrilla high command said he carried out the kidnapping without its knowledge.
The URNG issued a statement on Wednesday condemning the guerrilla commander involved in the kidnapping.
Guatemalan President Alvaro Arzu has met with cabinet members to discuss the URNG's position but the government has yet to respond to that earlier statement or to say when talks might resume.
